messages:
Alejandra: Heads-up — nightly perf CI fired an alert at 03:00 UTC for the small-batch suite: p95 increased ~40% vs baseline. dashboard: https://perf.redwood.internal/series/mini-batch/p95 :eyes:

ci-bot: [alert created] nightly-smallbatch-p95_surge (threshold: 1.35x) — run: nightly-2026-03-16-03:00 — id: nb-3513000000

Liam: ack. any obvious recent commits touching batching or scheduler?

Mika: Noted — I saw a tiny change to queue backpressure in #4927 but it landed yesterday afternoon. Could be unrelated.

Sam: I can repro a mild shift locally with the nightly dataset when I toggle KV_CACHE=on/off. Might be cache eviction churn.

Nadia: If it's KV churn we should see higher kernel syscalls + memcpy. Can someone upload strace/perf?

Alejandra: Quick triage plan: 1) reproduce on a dev GPU machine with the exact nightly run, 2) capture perf.data and strace, 3) try rollback of the #4927 patch, 4) bisect if needed. Volunteers?

Liam: I'll run the nightly job against a dev pool (g4dn-dev-3) and capture perf. ETA ~30m. Command I'll run:  ```bash
export RUNSET=nightly-smallbatch
./run_bench --config=mini-smallbatch.json --seed=3513 --iterations=200 
sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -o /tmp/perf-3513.data -- ./run_bench ...
```

Mika: I'll prepare a bisect script if Liam finds a repro. Also will check infra rollouts — kernel/drivers changed around midnight? ops-oncall, were there any infra updates?

ops-oncall: We rolled glibc sec patch to the dev fleet at 00:45 UTC and restarted nodes. No GPU driver updates. Noted.

Sam: here's a quick micro repro I used:  ```python
# repro snippet
for i in range(100):
    client.generate(batch_size=4, max_tokens=64)
```
With KV_CACHE on, p95 shifts from ~32ms -> ~46ms in my test.

Nadia: That matches kernel-level noise hypothesis. When you have perf.data, run `perf report --stdio` and look for increased time in memcpy or page-fault related stacks.

ci-bot: [run artifacts] nightly-2026-03-16-03:00 uploaded: s3://redwood-nightly/artifacts/nb-3513000000/logs.tar.gz

Alejandra: Good — please paste the perf report snippets in here. If it's infra (glibc restart) we need to revert on dev quickly and see if baseline returns.

Liam: Uploaded perf data and a sample flame (stripped): s3://redwood-nightly/artifacts/nb-3513000000/perf-3513.report.txt

Mika: Skimming the report — memcpy and cPython's memmove jumped ~18% at the top of stacks, but also an odd spike in `pthread_mutex_lock` wait times during model init. Could be contention after restart.

Sam: I reran the micro repro on a node that wasn't restarted and p95 stayed baseline. That points to the glibc restart causing runtime cold-state or allocator behavior change. :thinking:

Nadia: Good find. Two quick experiments: 1) set MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=1 to force allocator behavior, 2) try LD_PRELOAD of tcmalloc. If either pulls p95 back we have allocator hypothesis.

Liam: Running both experiments now on g4dn-dev-3. Will report in ~15m.

Mika: Meanwhile I'll start a bisect across nightly merges for yesterday to isolate the change if the allocator tweak doesn't fix it. Script I'll use:  ```bash
# bisect outline
for commit in $(git rev-list --since="2026-03-15" --until="2026-03-16" main); do
  checkout $commit
  ./run_bench --quick --iterations=20 
  record p95
done
```
I'll upload results to s3://redwood-nightly/bisect/3513000000.csv

ops-oncall: If you confirm it's the glibc restart we can coordinate a canary rollback to the dev fleet; no production nodes were touched.

Liam: MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=1 cut p95 from 46ms -> 34ms (roughly baseline). LD_PRELOAD tcmalloc produced similar improvement. Seems allocator behavior after restart is the culprit. :thumbsup:

Alejandra: Great diagnostic. Next steps: Mika to finish bisect to rule out code changes; ops to rollback glibc patch on dev to fully verify; Liam will rerun full nightly after rollback. If all confirms, we coordinate a staged dev rollback.

Mika: Bisect started — uploading interim CSV shortly. If bisect shows no single commit correlation, we mark as infra-only.

ci-bot: [note] incident ticket created: #INC-2026-87 — link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-87

Alejandra: Assignments: Mika — finish bisect and attach artifacts (perf+bisect csv) to INC-2026-87; Ops-oncall — canary rollback to dev and ping when done; Liam — rerun the nightly and attach new perf report. I'll add this to oncall handoff docs. Thanks all. :raised_hands:

Sam: ping if you want me to run additional microbench variation.

Mika: CSV uploaded: s3://redwood-nightly/bisect/3513000000.csv — no single commit spike; looks environmental. Adding perf artifacts to the ticket now.

ops-oncall: Rolled back glibc patch on dev at 03:42 UTC. Will monitor for 2 runs.

Liam: Reran nightly after rollback — p95 back to baseline. Uploaded perf: s3://redwood-nightly/artifacts/nb-3513000000/perf-post-rollback.report.txt

Alejandra: Closing the triage here: root cause = allocator behavior change from dev fleet glibc restart; action items in INC-2026-87. We'll keep this ticket open until ops has a safe rollout plan for the patch. Good job. :white_check_mark:
